newsitem.title: SENEGAL: New gold prospecting permits in demand in Senegal.
newsitem.headline: New gold prospecting permits in demand in Senegal.

text.p: Senegal hopes to be in a position to issue up to six new gold prospecting permits by the end of May but at least 14 companies have already put in requests, Senegal's director of Mines said Tuesday.
"Fourteen companies have asked for gold permits to Senegal. We hope by the end of May to have a general council of mines and figure out how many permits we can give," Abdoulaye Dia told Reuters.
"But we will be in a position to give only five or six new permits," Dia said.
Canadian company Barrick Gold Corp was among the 14 seeking permits, he added.

A study by Australian firm Paget Mining Ltd has confirmed the potential of a deposit at Sabodala, 700 km east of Dakar, by raising its projection of proven reserves to 30 tonnes of gold from 13 tonnes.
In recent months, Senegal has issued 20 exploration permits to such major international companies as Ashanti Goldfields Co. of Ghana and South Africa's Anglo-American and Randgold.
